note: Antigua and Barbuda, read on 2026-10-30 in the Immigration and Passport Act, Cap. 208, as the Government's laws site (laws.gov.ag) publishes it in the Revised Laws. A permit to enter may be issued on the Chief Immigration Officer's authority to anyone not a prohibited immigrant, in writing and on conditions prescribed by regulations; the Officer may ask for evidence of good character, medical certificates, proof the applicant can maintain himself and his dependants, full particulars of any gainful occupation he proposes to engage in, a bond, a deposit for repatriation and particulars (s. 21(1)-(2)); permission may be limited in duration and given on conditions (s. 21(3)). Being the one permit for any purpose, it is written as `general`. A person wanting to stay beyond a permit's expiry presents himself to the Chief Immigration Officer before it ends and is dealt with as if entering for the first time (s. 22(1)), so it is renewable; such a later permit costs $50 for citizens of the CARICOM states the section names and of Anguilla, the British Virgin Islands and Montserrat, $100 for anyone else (s. 22(2)), a fee for a permit after an earlier one and not the first's, so no fee is written. The Act's own text names no term, decision time, permanent residence, or which work the permit allows. The site's copy carries no date of revision, and later amending acts and the fee regulations weren't found; the Labour Code's work permit (the work engine's) and the Department of Immigration's own site (immigration.gov.ag, which doesn't resolve) weren't read here.

sources.title: Laws of Antigua and Barbuda, Cap. 208, The Immigration and Passport Act
sources.said: a permit to enter Antigua and Barbuda may be issued on the authority of the Chief Immigration Officer to any person not being a prohibited immigrant. ... such permit shall be in writing and shall be subject to such conditions as may be prescribed by regulations. ... to provide full particulars of any gainful occupation in which he proposes to engage; ... be limited in duration to a time specified in the permission; ... Antigua and Barbuda after the expiration of a permit granted under this Act, he shall, before such expiration, present himself in person to the Chief Immigration Officer and shall be dealt with as if he were an immigrant entering Antigua and Barbuda for the first time. ... of one hundred dollars in the case of citizens of the United Kingdom other than those specified in item ( 6 ) above and of any other person.
